newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka to award oil tanks contract in June.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka to award oil tanks contract in June.

text.p: Sri Lanka will this month award contracts to rebuild oil storage tanks destroyed in a Tamil Tiger rebel attack in 1995, a government minister told parliament on Tuesday.
Deputy Minister of Irrigation and Power Piyasena Gamage said in a reply to a question that the contracts worth $41.1 million were expected to be awarded by the end of June.

Officials of state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corporation said last month that companies from five countries -- Japan, South Korea, China, Singapore and Italy -- have tendered to rebuild the tanks destroyed during a daring attack by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in October 1995 at the two main oil depots in Colombo.
The rebels damaged or destroyed up to 16 tanks in the attack.
The successful bidder will rebuild oil tanks at the Orugodwatta and Kolonnawa oil storage facilities in Colombo. CPC officials have said that reconstruction work will begin in September.
The Asian Development Bank has given a soft loan of $24 million for the reconstruction. The CPC has to find the remaining funds locally.
